result:
All 26 tests compile and run; 25 pass and 1 fails, revealing a genuine bug.

**Bug found:** `testPropertiesAreAllProcessedIndependently` fails. In `Parser.processProperties` (`src/java/org/apache/commons/cli/Parser.java:282-289`), when a no-arg option's property value isn't `yes`/`true`/`1`, the code does `break` instead of `continue`. The comment right above it even says the intent is just to skip *that* option ("if the value is not yes, true or 1 then don't add the option to the CommandLine"), but `break` aborts the entire `Enumeration` loop, silently dropping every property that comes after it — including unrelated options that take arguments. My test sets `f=false` (a flag) followed by `x=hello` (an arg option) in a deterministic order and shows `x` never gets applied because of the early `break`.

The other 25 tests pass, covering: null-argument handling, simple/arg options, missing-argument and unrecognized-option errors, optional-arg non-consumption, singular/plural `MissingOptionException` messages, required options and required `OptionGroup` satisfaction/violation, `AlreadySelectedException`, `-`/`--` edge cases (including the single-`-`-dropped-when-stopping case and duplicate `--`), `stopAtNonOption` behavior, quote-stripping, CLI-71 value-clearing between parses, and `Properties`-based option filling/overriding.
